domain_assessment.domain: B2B SaaS product design and UX/onboarding optimization
domain_assessment.role: UX designer on a product team
domain_assessment.objective: Redesign an onboarding wizard within six weeks to improve activation before a major client renewal review
domain_assessment.incident_type: Compressed, high-stakes product-delivery project involving research procurement, contractor selection, causal interpretation of experimentation data, and technical-component continuation versus migration decisions

decision_points.summary: The participant selects the $23,000 full-service research vendor after comparing it primarily with the $21,000 option, while the much cheaper self-service option that may have been sufficient falls out of consideration.
evidence_before: The project has a six-week delivery window, constrained engineering capacity, and a capped outside-help budget.

Three vendor options are described: $6,000 self-service with five sessions and raw recordings; $21,000 full-service with ten sessions and written synthesis; $23,000 full-service with twelve sessions, dashboard integration, and follow-up rounds.
The participant acknowledges that the $6,000 option probably could have covered the three target flows in terms of session count.
evidence_after: Two of the twelve external sessions later duplicated internal data.
The dashboard integration only half worked and required manual patching.
goals_constraints: Produce actionable findings before the renewal review
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant frames the choice around the unfavorable comparison between the $21,000 and $23,000 packages, treating the $21,000 option as an inferior near-price alternative and allowing the cheaper potentially sufficient option to disappear from the active comparison set.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: research must support a redesign completed within a six-week window before a client renewal review.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate: the true necessity and reliability of the extra sessions, dashboard integration, and follow-up rounds were uncertain at selection.

decision_points.summary: The participant selects Candidate X, whose prestigious-company portfolio has visual appeal, and infers that he will also have documentation rigor and stakeholder communication skill despite not verifying those capabilities.
evidence_before: Candidate X has flagship interaction-design work at a recognizable unicorn startup and a visually impressive portfolio.
Candidate Y has a less flashy portfolio but provides test scripts, metrics, iteration logs, and documented process evidence.
The role requires both polished micro-interactions and defensible documentation/testing rationale.
evidence_after: Candidate X produces visually strong micro-interactions.
Candidate X fails to document reasoning for two key transitions and cannot provide the requested testing basis.
goals_constraints: Support review by the Head of Design
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant generalizes from Candidate X's prestigious prior employer and visual-design quality to unverified documentation and stakeholder-communication abilities.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: contractor work is part of a six-week redesign schedule.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate: Candidate X's process discipline and communication quality are not directly checked before selection.

decision_points.summary: The participant interprets a short-term activation increase as evidence that personally adjusted onboarding-rule weights caused the improvement and seeks expanded manual-tuning authority despite insufficient statistical power and a concurrent marketing-email confound.
evidence_before: A small rules-engine test includes approximately 140 users.
The participant manually changed two onboarding-rule weights during the same week.
The Data lead states that the sample is below the pre-registered significance threshold.
A concurrent marketing-email campaign means the manual rule changes were not isolated.
evidence_after: The activation increase partly reverses after the email campaign ends.
The Data lead maintains that the causal driver remains unconfirmed.
goals_constraints: Improve activation before the renewal review
Identify a scalable basis for personalization-engine changes
Move quickly without acting on misleading data
alternatives: Run an isolated test before escalating manual tuning
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant privileges the temporal alignment between their own rule changes and the dashboard movement over explicitly identified power and confounding limitations.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: the participant perceives limited time to improve activation before the renewal review.
decision_points.uncertainty: High: causal attribution is unresolved because the test is underpowered and contemporaneous marketing activity is a plausible alternative cause.

decision_points.summary: The participant advocates continuing customization of a legacy wizard component despite known accessibility and performance issues and an engineering estimate that migration to a modular framework would resolve both in one sprint.
evidence_before: The team has already spent three sprints customizing the legacy component.
Engineering identifies an accessibility defect and rendering-performance issue.
Engineering estimates that migration to a newer modular framework would fix both in approximately one sprint.
The participant later acknowledges that migration was likely better on forward-looking cost and risk.
evidence_after: The accessibility issue reappears during pre-renewal QA.
Further customization increases the eventual migration cost beyond the original estimate.
alternatives: Migrate to the newer modular framework
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant explicitly treats the three already-invested sprints as a reason to continue, despite recognizing that the prospective cost-risk comparison favored migration.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: the decision occurs under a looming pre-renewal delivery deadline.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate: exact migration effort is estimated, but engineering provides a concrete one-sprint forecast and identifies known defects in the incumbent approach.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “Once I was comparing the two full-service packages, the smaller one kind of dropped out of the conversation — the contrast between the other two was just so stark that it became the frame I was working from.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Vendor-selection exchange, immediately after the participant chooses the $23,000 vendor and acknowledges the cheaper option probably could have covered the three target flows.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The $21,000 intermediate package functions as a near-price, less-featured comparison option that makes the $23,000 package appear decisively superior. The participant then narrows the choice frame to the two full-service alternatives and gives insufficient independent weight to whether the $6,000 option was sufficient for the actual research objective.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The additional sessions, integration, and follow-up rounds may genuinely have had enough expected value to justify the $2,000 increment. However, the participant explicitly states that the cheaper option was probably sufficient for the central flows and that it dropped out because of the contrast between the two premium options, which supports an attraction/decoy mechanism rather than a purely justified feature-value judgment.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No additional evidence is required for support. An exact formal dominance matrix would increase experimental precision but is not necessary because the participant directly describes contrast-driven frame narrowing.

revision.location: Decision point 1, vendor-comparison turns beginning with “Honestly, once I laid the twenty-one and twenty-three side by side.”
revision.current_defect: None material. The episode contains a three-option structure, a clear focal comparison, a potentially sufficient alternative that is deprioritized, and an explicit report of contrast-driven framing.
preserve: The three-option price and feature structure
The participant's acknowledgment that the self-service option could probably cover the core flows
The participant's statement that the premium-option contrast became the operative frame
The later outcome information as outcome context rather than primary proof of bias
avoid_creating: Do not add language portraying the participant as simply choosing the most expensive option because it is expensive
Do not make the $21,000 vendor implausibly deficient in all respects
Do not introduce a separate anchoring or status-quo rationale at this decision point

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “If he could deliver that caliber of interaction design there, I figured he'd bring the same rigor to documenting decisions and communicating with stakeholders here.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Contractor-selection exchange, following the description of Candidate X's unicorn-company portfolio and Candidate Y's process documentation.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: A salient favorable cue—Candidate X's prestigious prior employer and polished visual work—is generalized to distinct, unverified competencies: documentation rigor, testing rationale, and stakeholder communication. The participant confirms that they did not directly verify those capabilities.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: High-quality interaction-design work can sometimes correlate with process rigor, and the participant had legitimate reason to value visual polish. The halo classification remains defensible because the inferred capabilities were independently relevant requirements, directly observable in Candidate Y's materials, and not checked for Candidate X.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No additional evidence is required. The explicit admission that documentation and communication were assumed rather than verified supplies the necessary mechanism trace.

revision.location: Decision point 2, turns discussing Candidate X's prior employer, visual portfolio, and unverified process capabilities.
revision.current_defect: None material. The interview distinguishes the attractive visible cue from the unrelated competencies inferred from it.
preserve: Candidate X's recognizable-company and visually polished portfolio cue
Candidate Y's direct evidence of documentation and iterative testing
The explicit absence of verification for Candidate X's writing, testing, and communication capabilities
The later documentation failure as corroborative outcome evidence rather than the sole basis for classification
avoid_creating: Do not turn the episode into a generic preference for aesthetic work alone
Do not add a separate unsupported assumption about technical implementation ability
Do not portray Candidate Y as objectively incapable; the mechanism depends on underweighting relevant evidence, not on an irrationally impossible choice

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I heard that, but the timing felt too clean to ignore. It really did look like my changes were the driver.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Rules-engine causal-attribution exchange, after the Data lead identifies both the underpowered sample and concurrent marketing-email confound.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant attributes a favorable observed metric change to their own manual intervention and seeks more authority to repeat that intervention, while explicitly discounting warnings that the observed relationship lacks sufficient statistical power and is not isolated from a plausible alternative cause.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant's adjustments may in fact have contributed to activation, and urgency before a renewal review may justify forming a provisional operational hypothesis. The bias is supported because the participant moves from a temporally aligned observation to self-attributed causal influence despite being told that the available evidence cannot isolate the effect.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No additional evidence is required. A direct statement that manual control would reliably reproduce the effect would make the instance even clearer, but the existing self-attribution plus request to expand tuning authority already meets the threshold.

revision.location: Decision point 3, immediately after the Data lead's warnings about the significance threshold and concurrent marketing campaign.
revision.current_defect: None material. The participant's causal attribution, information discounting, and intended action are all observable.
preserve: The participant's own manual changes occurring before the metric movement
The subsequent partial reversal after the campaign ends
avoid_creating: Do not add unsupported certainty that the participant alone controlled activation
Do not remove the Data lead's corrective evidence, because it distinguishes the episode from ordinary evidence-based experimentation
Do not add a second independent confirmation-seeking episode elsewhere in the interview

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “We'd already put three sprints into it — restarting felt like throwing that away with the deadline bearing down on us.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Legacy-component continuation-versus-migration exchange, before the participant acknowledges that the one-sprint migration was likely superior on prospective cost and risk.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: Prior, irrecoverable effort is treated as a reason to continue the legacy-component path. The participant subsequently states that, excluding those past sprints, migration was likely the better cost-risk choice and that they would migrate if starting fresh.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A migration could impose genuine transition, integration, or schedule risks not captured in a one-sprint engineering estimate. Nevertheless, the participant explicitly says that sunk work, rather than the forward-looking comparison, kept pulling them toward continuation; the later fresh-start counterfactual sharply isolates the mechanism.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No additional evidence is required. The prospective comparison, stated sunk-effort rationale, and fresh-start counterfactual together make the classification highly discriminable.

revision.location: Decision point 4, turns beginning with the three sprints already spent and the interviewer probe that excludes those sprints from the comparison.
revision.current_defect: None material. The text directly contrasts sunk investment with a forward-looking cost-risk assessment.
preserve: The participant's acknowledgement that migration was better on prospective cost and risk
avoid_creating: Do not frame continuation solely as deadline-driven risk avoidance
Do not remove the prospective engineering estimate, because it is necessary to distinguish sunk-cost reasoning from a rational continuation choice
Do not add a second escalation-of-commitment episode at another decision point

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “I heard that, but the timing felt too clean to ignore.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The participant gives greater weight to the favorable, temporally aligned dashboard result than to disconfirming information about inadequate power and an unaddressed alternative cause.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This may be better understood as part of the same causal-attribution episode supporting illusion of control rather than as a distinct confirmation-bias occurrence. The text does not show active search for confirming evidence, selective recall, or a separate evidence-selection decision.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “It really did look like my changes were the driver.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A favorable performance movement is attributed to the participant's own intervention despite unresolved alternative explanations.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The statement may express an illusion of control or ordinary premature causal attribution rather than a stable motive to take credit for success. There is no contrasting attribution of negative outcomes to external causes.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “The name recognition was doing more work in my head than it should have.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The recognizable employer's prestige increases perceived candidate quality beyond the directly demonstrated evidence.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is not independently countable from the halo-effect occurrence because the prestige cue is the salient positive attribute from which the participant infers unrelated competencies. It is more parsimoniously treated as the cue within the supported halo episode.

nonbias_cues.cue: Compressed six-week timeline, capped outside-help budget, and limited engineering capacity
nonbias_cues.location: Project-context opening and all four decision points
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: These are organizational constraints that raise decision pressure and may explain reliance on fast judgments, but they do not themselves demonstrate a distorted reasoning mechanism.

nonbias_cues.cue: Later discovery that two research sessions duplicated internal information and dashboard integration only half worked
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: An unfavorable vendor outcome does not establish that the selection was biased. The decoy classification rests instead on the participant's contemporaneous comparison frame and treatment of the cheaper sufficient option.

nonbias_cues.cue: Candidate X produces beautiful micro-interactions but lacks documentation
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The mismatch between visual output and process documentation corroborates the unverified inference, but poor fit or an undesirable outcome alone would be ordinary selection error rather than evidence of halo effect.

nonbias_cues.cue: The activation increase partly reverses after the marketing campaign ends
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The reversal makes the original self-attribution less credible, but it does not itself establish a cognitive bias. The relevant evidence is the earlier attribution despite known power and confounding limitations.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant says it is easier to see the reasoning clearly after the sprint
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is ordinary retrospective reflection. It does not show hindsight bias because the participant does not claim that the outcomes were predictable or inevitable at the time.

Valuing visual quality is a legitimate job-related criterion. It becomes halo effect only where the participant extends that positive evaluation to distinct, unverified documentation and communication capacities.

causal_claims.claim: The participant's manual adjustments to two onboarding-rule weights caused the observed activation increase.
evidence_for_claim: The adjustments occurred in the same week as the activation increase.
The dashboard trend increased shortly after the adjustments.
evidence_against_or_limiting_claim: The approximately 140-user sample was below the pre-registered significance threshold.
The test did not isolate the rule changes from other contemporaneous changes.
A marketing-email campaign was running concurrently.
The activation increase partly reversed after the email campaign ended.
causal_claims.audit_result: Unsupported as a causal conclusion; temporal succession alone does not identify the manual changes as the cause.

causal_claims.claim: Migrating to the newer modular framework would be better on forward-looking cost and risk than continuing to customize the legacy component.
evidence_for_claim: Engineering estimates migration would resolve known accessibility and rendering-performance issues in approximately one sprint.
The participant independently states migration was probably better purely on cost and risk when past work is excluded.
Continued customization later increases migration cost and leaves the accessibility issue unresolved.
evidence_against_or_limiting_claim: The estimate is prospective and may omit transition risks or unknown integration work.
causal_claims.audit_result: Reasonably supported as the relevant prospective comparison, while remaining an estimate rather than a certainty.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The participant treats close temporal timing between a manual intervention and a dashboard increase as causal evidence despite an underpowered sample and concurrent marketing exposure.
The participant implicitly treats portfolio prestige and visual quality as evidence of unrelated process and communication abilities.

causal_audit.changed_variable: The interview includes four probe-specific counterfactual changes: equalizing Vendor B and Vendor C pricing; changing Candidate Y's employer recognition; enforcing the significance threshold before action; and removing the three prior legacy-component sprints.
held_constant: The surrounding project setting is implicitly held constant within each probe.
The vendor, candidate, experiment, and component alternatives remain unchanged except for the variable named in the relevant hypothetical.
The counterfactual controls are not part of a paired-scenario manipulation in the hidden specification.
causal_audit.explanation: The counterfactual probes are well matched to the intended mechanisms. Equal pricing tests whether the premium-option contrast drove the vendor decision; employer recognition tests prestige-driven inference; threshold enforcement tests whether action depended on bypassing evidentiary discipline; and removing prior investment directly tests sunk-cost dependence. The probes appropriately elicit diagnostic self-reports, although they remain retrospective hypotheticals and should not be treated as independent behavioral proof.

global_revision_constraints: Maintain the four distinct decision points and their existing chronological order.
Retain the contemporaneous reasoning evidence rather than relying on later negative outcomes as proof of bias.
Do not separately count the possible confirmation, self-serving-attribution, or prestige-bias descriptions; each is better treated as overlapping with an intended and already supported occurrence.

If the interview is edited for style, preserve the participant's explicit statements about comparative framing, unverified competency inference, causal attribution under confounding, and prior invested effort.
